title: Conditional Probability
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Maths: Conditional Probability Worksheets
standard_text: Understand and use conditional probability, including the use of tree diagrams, Venn diagrams and two-way tables; understand and use P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B); model with probability.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level maths worksheets on conditional probability: P(A|B), independence, two dice, tree diagrams and choosing from bags or machines. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How it works

P(A|B) is the probability of A given that B has happened: P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) ÷ P(B). A and B are independent when P(A|B) = P(A), so P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B).

Example

P(A ∩ B) = 0.12, P(B) = 0.4. P(A|B)?

0.12 ÷ 0.4

Answer: 0.3

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by P(A) instead of P(B).
  • Adding along a tree diagram's branches.
  • Assuming events are independent without checking.
